newsitem.title: USA: Tatham to take Q4 writedown.
newsitem.headline: Tatham to take Q4 writedown.

text.p: Tatham Offshore Inc said Monday that it expects to reserve the costs associated with its oil and gas developments in Ship Shoal Block 331 and Ewing Banks Block 91, resulting in a fourth quarter writedown of about $42 million.

Production related problems resulting from the completions of the three wellbores at Ship Shoal Block 331 have resulted in only a minimal amount of production from the property and the company has decided not to pursue further recompletion operations at this time, it said.

The Ewing Bank Block 914 2 well has been shut-in since May 1997 as a result of a downhole mechanical problem, and the company said it is still evaluating potential workover or recompletion possibilities for the well. However, it has decided to reserve the remaining costs associated with the Ewing Bank 914 2 well given its current non-productive status.

"Although we believe that there are further hydrocarbon development possibilities with both the Ship Shoal Block 331 and Ewing Bank Block 914 2 properties, we have chosen to focus our current activities and resources on the Sunday Silence project, offshore Louisiana, and the North Atlantic pipeline project located primarily offshore Nova Scotia and Newfoundland," Chairman and Chief Executive Thomas Tatham said in a statement.
As a result of the expected asset write-downs, Tatham said it anticipates that its common stock may no longer meet the listing requirements for the Nasdaq National Market.

In order to continue to meet the Nasdaq listing requirements, the company said it may seek to convert all or a portion of its current debt to common stock, exchange a portion of its assets for all or a portion of its debt or take other actions to increase its equity.
If Tatham's actions do not increase its equity, the company said it expects that its common stock will trade on the Nasdaq Small Cap market.

Tatham is an independent energy company engaged in the exploration, development and production of oil and gas reserves located offshore the United States in the Gulf of Mexico and offshore eastern Canada.
